AU.title: ABS Census — Special Short Form (SSF) / Household Form (HHF)
AU.description: Australia’s official homelessness estimates come from the Census. People not in a dwelling were usually interviewed with the paper Special Short Form (SSF) — a shortened Census Household Form (HHF) for people sleeping rough when field staff need to interview several people quickly. SSF was the primary method for NSW, Victoria, Tasmania, South Australia, and southern parts of WA and Queensland. NT and northern WA/Qld more often used the full HHF.
cues: Special Short Form (SSF) — shortened paper interview for people sleeping rough / not in a dwelling
Census Household Form (HHF) — full household form; also used in some rough-sleeping interviews (esp. NT, northern WA/Qld)
Where did you sleep on Census night? (SSF Q1) — street, landmark, suburb, postcode
Usual address can be recorded as none when someone has nowhere they usually live

AU:Darwin.title: ABS Census — Household Form (HHF) primary for NT rough sleeping
AU:Darwin.description: In the Northern Territory, people not in a dwelling were primarily enumerated by interview using the paper or online Census Household Form (HHF), not the Special Short Form.
cues: Census Household Form (HHF) — primary NT instrument for people not in a dwelling
Usual address / ‘none’ responses help classify temporary stays and rough sleeping
Supported accommodation and boarding-house lists also feed the homelessness estimate
National estimates still combine SSF + HHF + administrative lists across Australia

US.title: HUD Point-in-Time (PIT) Count — model survey tools
US.description: US Continuums of Care run an annual Point-in-Time count of sheltered and unsheltered homelessness on a single January night. HUD publishes optional model PIT survey instruments and a methodology guide; CoCs may adapt them but must collect HUD’s minimum required data elements.
cues: Where did you sleep last night? (shelter / outdoors / vehicle / other)
Household type — individual, adult-only, or family with children
Length of time homeless and whether homelessness has been long-term / repeated (chronic)
Veteran status, disability, and other HUD subpopulation questions on model interview forms

US:New York City.title: NYC CoC (NY-600) Point-in-Time Count
US:New York City.description: New York City’s Continuum of Care reports sheltered and unsheltered PIT figures to HUD using the national PIT framework. Official results are in HUD’s CoC PopSub reports.
US:New York City.urlLabel: HUD CoC PopSub NY-600 New York City 2024 (PDF)
cues: HUD PIT night-of-count categories: emergency shelter, transitional housing, Safe Haven, unsheltered
Local street and shelter count operations still map to HUD model survey themes
Household type and chronic homelessness flags required for HUD reporting
Subpopulations: veterans, serious mental illness, substance use, DV survivors

US:Los Angeles.title: Los Angeles City & County CoC (CA-600) Point-in-Time Count
US:Los Angeles.description: Los Angeles City & County CoC conducts the local PIT under HUD standards. Results appear in the CA-600 CoC PopSub.
US:Los Angeles.urlLabel: HUD CoC PopSub CA-600 Los Angeles 2024 (PDF)
cues: Sheltered vs unsheltered on the designated PIT night
Interview or observation tools adapted from HUD model PIT surveys
Chronic homelessness, veteran, and disability subpopulation items
Vehicle, tent, and makeshift-structure locations often flagged in unsheltered counts

US:Chicago.title: Chicago CoC (IL-510) Point-in-Time Count
US:Chicago.description: Chicago’s CoC PIT follows HUD’s HIC/PIT data-collection notice; published totals are in the IL-510 PopSub.
cues: Night-of-count shelter roster + unsheltered street count
HUD-required household and subpopulation fields
Length of time homeless / chronic criteria
Model PIT interview themes: sleeping location, veterans, disability

US:Seattle.title: Seattle/King County CoC (WA-500) Point-in-Time Count
US:Seattle.description: Seattle/King County reports PIT results to HUD under national count standards (WA-500 CoC PopSub).
US:Seattle.urlLabel: HUD CoC PopSub WA-500 Seattle/King County 2024 (PDF)
cues: Sheltered and unsheltered PIT on the CoC’s designated night
HUD model survey themes adapted locally
Chronic homelessness and household-type reporting
Veterans and disability-related subpopulation questions

CA.title: Everyone Counts — Survey on Homelessness (PiT Count)
CA.description: Canada’s nationally coordinated Point-in-Time Count (“Everyone Counts”) combines a one-night enumeration with a Survey on Homelessness (core screening + 15 standardized questions).
cues: Core screening: where are you staying tonight / did you sleep unsheltered or in shelter?
Demographics — age, gender, Indigenous identity, veteran status
Reasons for housing loss and how long you’ve been homeless
Income sources, health conditions, and service needs (core survey block)

GB.title: England rough sleeping snapshot + Rough Sleeping Questionnaire
GB.description: England’s official autumn rough-sleeping snapshot is a single-night local-authority count or evidence-based estimate (DELTA return). Separately, MHCLG’s Rough Sleeping Questionnaire interviews people with recent rough-sleeping experience.
cues: Single ‘typical night’ between 1 Oct and 30 Nov (count or multi-agency estimate)
DELTA return: totals plus age, gender, nationality breakdowns
Rough Sleeping Questionnaire: homelessness history, support needs, public-service use
Statutory homelessness (H-CLIC) applications are a separate administrative series

NZ.title: Stats NZ severe housing deprivation (Census) estimates
NZ.description: New Zealand’s official homelessness-related measure is severe housing deprivation estimated from the Census (and admin data) — not a separate street-survey form.
NZ.urlLabel: Stats NZ severe housing deprivation methodology (2023 Census)
cues: Derived from Census dwelling and household questions — not a dedicated ‘homeless form’
Without shelter / improvised / sleeping rough classifications
Temporary non-private accommodation (e.g. night shelters, motels used as temporary housing)
Severe crowding and lacking basic amenities indicators

IE.title: PASS emergency-accommodation count (monthly)
IE.description: Ireland’s published monthly homelessness figures come from the Pathway Accommodation and Support System (PASS) — an administrative count of people in funded emergency accommodation, not a public street-interview questionnaire.
IE.urlLabel: Pathway Accommodation and Support System (PASS) overview
cues: PASS bed-night / emergency accommodation placements (Section 10 funded)
Adults and children in private emergency, supported, and temporary accommodation
Not a full rough-sleeper census — street counts are separate where done
Monthly Department reports summarise PASS extracts rather than a public form

DE.title: Destatis Statistik untergebrachter wohnungsloser Personen
DE.description: Germany’s federal statistic counts people accommodated because of homelessness on a reference date. It is institutional reporting, not a public street questionnaire.
cues: Reference-date count of people placed in municipal / provider accommodation
Provider and municipal reporting via official statistical channels
Excludes many rough sleepers and hidden stays with friends/family from this series
Biennial federal homelessness report adds wider estimates beyond the core statistic

FR.title: INSEE Enquête Sans Domicile
FR.description: France’s Sans Domicile survey interviews people using accommodation and meal services (short multilingual + longer French questionnaires).
cues: Short multilingual questionnaire + longer French questionnaire
Sampled via accommodation and food-aid services (not a door-to-door census)
Housing situation the night before / usual sleeping place
Demographics, pathways into homelessness, and service use
